page: Microsoft Azure M176-88bds_4_v3 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MBDSMediumMemoryv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 88 dedicated vCPUs powered by x86_64 Intel Xeon 8473C processors operating at a clock speed of 4.0 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 44 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, 105 MB of L3 cache, and 3892.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 44.23 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, the instance is equipped with 8192 GB of local disk capacity and is Premium Storage capable. It does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance in memory bandwidth and database operations. Large-block read-only memory bandwidth reaches 419.61 GB/sec, and write bandwidth reaches 181.06 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. This high memory throughput is complemented by strong multi-core CPU performance, with a Passmark CPU score of 94,306.2 and a multi-core stress-ng score of 85,961.54. The system also excels in database operations, achieving a top-tier Passmark database score of 34,697.66 and a static web serving throughput of 101.83 GB/sec. Single-core performance is moderate by comparison, with stress-ng single-core and bzip3 single-threaded decompression scoring in the average tier.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server type offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads, trading off GPU acceleration for massive RAM capacity and substantial local storage. The inclusion of advanced instruction sets, such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), enables strong performance in specialized tasks like cryptography and vector calculations without requiring dedicated accelerators. This profile is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise relational databases, heavy data-compilation pipelines, and memory-intensive analytical workloads.
